newsitem.title: INDIA: India Reliance shareholders overjoyed with bonus.
newsitem.headline: India Reliance shareholders overjoyed with bonus.

text.p: Hundreds of shareholders clapped and cheered on Thursday as Dhirubhai Ambani, chief of India's largest private sector firm, Reliance Industries, announced it would issue one bonus share for each share held.

"I would like to announce my dear shareholders I am delighted to report to you that after due deliberation and considering your suggestions, the board has recommended a bonus issue in the ratio of 1:1," Ambani said.
Reliance began as a commodities trading firm in 1958 and built itself into a petrochemical and textile giant.
Shares of Reliance Industries Ltd soared 15.5 rupees, or 4.3 percent, to 382 after the announcement.
The announcement followed a brief board meeting after the firm's two-and-a-half-hour-long annual general meeting ended. But shareholders waited in their seats to hear the news.
Ambani said he had delayed the board meeting in order to canvass shareholders' opinions on the bonus ratio.

"We will put the curtain down, meet and discuss for 10 or 15 minutes and then come back and announce the ratio recommended by you board," Ambani told the meeting. "I hope you will support me in this approach."
Most of Reliance's 2.6 million Indian shareholders had set their hearts on a 1:1 ratio for the bonus issue, the first in 14 years. Traders had expected a ratio of 3:5, as in 1983.
"Let the rivers of bonus and dividends flow," shareholder Ashalata Maheshwari had said a few minutes earlier while addressing the meeting earlier.

Nitin Jhaveri, another "member of the Reliance family", as most shareholders described themselves, said he was concerned that the firm's equity was held mostly by foreign institutional investors and out of the reach of the Indian middle-class.
"It should remain within the purchasing power of the Indian," Jhaveri said, justifying his demand for a 1:1 ratio.
"It should not be more than 1:1," he added, "but investors will not be satisfied with less."

Dinesh Lakhani of Surat in western Gujarat, Ambani's home state, sounded a note of caution, recommending a 3:5 share issue ratio. "Everybody would like a 1:1 ratio, but you should keep something for the silver jubilee," referring to the company's 25th anniversary as a listed company in 2003.

Ambani told investors Reliance would announce share buy back plans after the federal government had passed a new Companies Act. "The moment the rule is announced, we will announce the buyback of shares," he said.
